skill.name: agile-product-owner
skill.description: Create INVEST-oriented user stories, acceptance criteria, heuristic estimates, priorities, and capacity-based sprint plans from epic scope.
skill.summary: Turn epic scope into structured stories and capacity-based sprint plans.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting around documented Python commands. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 23 uses Markdown backticks to format a documented Python command. It does not execute a shell or interpolate input.
Line 24 uses Markdown backticks to format the sprint command and its capacity placeholder. It contains no executable Ruby or shell construct.

content.user_title: Build Better Agile Backlogs and Sprint Plans
content.value_statement: Product owners spend significant time shaping epics into consistent, estimable stories. This skill creates structured stories and capacity-based sprint plans with repeatable heuristics.
actual_capabilities: Converts epic scope items into user stories for four built-in persona types.
Creates five acceptance criteria covering success, validation, errors, performance, and keyboard access.
Assigns story points and priority labels using keyword-based rules.
Checks six INVEST attributes with simple deterministic heuristics.
Builds capacity-constrained sprint commitments and identifies stretch candidates.
Formats detailed stories, sprint results, and backlog summaries for terminal output.
limitations: The command-line interface uses a built-in sample epic and does not accept custom epic data.
Estimation, priority, and INVEST results rely on keywords rather than team evidence or human judgment.
The tool does not persist backlogs or integrate with project management systems.
It does not calculate historical velocity despite the source description mentioning velocity tracking.

use_cases.title: Draft an Initial Backlog
use_cases.description: Turn an epic scope into consistently formatted stories before team refinement.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sprint Options
use_cases.description: Create a capacity-based commitment and a separate list of stretch candidates.

use_cases.title: Review Requirement Quality
use_cases.description: Use acceptance criteria and INVEST checks to identify stories needing clarification.

prompt_templates.title: Create One User Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one user story for [feature] and [persona]. Include a concise title, narrative, five acceptance criteria, priority, points, and INVEST checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a single, clearly scoped feature.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down an Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Break [epic name] into stories for [personas]. Use these scope items: [scope]. Add technical enablers for [requirements].
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a draft backlog from known epic scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize this backlog and propose a sprint for [capacity] points. Separate committed and stretch stories, then report utilization: [backlog].
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a capacity-based sprint planning option.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Refine a Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these stories against INVEST: [stories]. Flag heuristic assumptions, improve acceptance criteria, identify dependencies, and propose a capacity-based sprint plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced quality review before team refinement.

output_examples.input: Create a story for an end user exporting dashboard data.
output_examples.output: Export Dashboard Data. As an End User, I want to export dashboard data so that I can work efficiently. Priority: low. Points: three.

output_examples.input: Plan a sprint with 20 points from a prioritized backlog.
output_examples.output: Sprint capacity: 20 points. Committed work totals 18 points with 90 percent utilization. Eligible overflow appears as stretch work.

output_examples.input: Check whether a story about a possible future search feature meets INVEST.
output_examples.output: The story needs refinement. Its uncertain wording fails the testability check, while its short scope remains estimable and small.

best_practices: Treat generated stories as refinement drafts and validate them with delivery teams and stakeholders.
Replace heuristic estimates with team estimates based on technical context and historical performance.
Provide explicit personas, scope items, constraints, and technical requirements before generating a backlog.
anti_patterns: Do not treat keyword-based priority as a substitute for product value and risk assessment.
Do not commit generated stories before reviewing dependencies, feasibility, and acceptance criteria.
Do not use the sample command-line output as evidence of historical velocity.

faq.question: Does this skill create custom stories from command-line input?
faq.answer: Not directly. The included command-line interface runs a built-in sample epic unless the script is adapted.

faq.question: How are story points estimated?
faq.answer: The generator assigns one, three, eight, or thirteen points from keywords in each feature description.

faq.question: How does sprint planning work?
faq.answer: It sorts stories by priority and size, fills the stated capacity, and marks eligible overflow within 120 percent as stretch work.

faq.question: Does it integrate with Jira or other backlog tools?
faq.answer: No. The included implementation prints results and provides no project management integration.

faq.question: Are the INVEST checks authoritative?
faq.answer: No. They are simple heuristics that support discussion and require team review.

faq.question: Does it track team velocity over time?
faq.answer: No. It reports generated backlog totals and sprint utilization, but it stores no historical velocity data.
